findings.description: "the routing test asserts it" is inaccurate: the test checks a hardcoded list of 16 already-moved paths and cannot fail for a future extraction, so a dev who trusts it gets green tests with the new file non-critical. The same claim is in ADR 0092 line 112.
findings.body:
The new JSDoc says a future extraction out of a critical file needs its own `CRITICAL_AREAS` entry, and adds "(the routing test asserts it)". The ADR 0092 amendment makes the same claim at `docs/adr/0092-pup-routes-every-window-s-model-and-effort.md` line 112: "A future extraction out of a critical file needs its own entry; the routing test asserts it."

The test can't catch a missing entry for a future extraction. `src/core/routing-utils.test.ts` lines 71-91 is an `it.each` over 16 hardcoded paths that have already moved. For each path it checks that `tierForScope([path])` returns `'critical'` and that some `CRITICAL_AREAS` glob matches. `routing-utils.test.ts` is the only test that imports `CRITICAL_AREAS`, and no guard test scans `src/core/{types,constants,errors}/`.

**How it goes wrong:** someone moves types out of a critical file into a new `src/core/types/foo.types.ts`. The new path isn't in the list, so the suite stays green. The sentence told them a missing entry would be caught, so they add neither the entry nor a test case. The file routes as standard tier, which is the regression #413 fixed.

Fix both places: say the test pins only the paths it lists, so the new path has to be added there as well as to `CRITICAL_AREAS`.

findings.suggestion:
* its files into `src/core/{types,constants,errors}/` are named beside it. A
 * future extraction out of a critical file needs its own entry here, and its
 * path added to the routing test's list, which pins only the paths it names.
